# Pragma Research

> Cadence is a deep real-time brain that learns from experience.

Pragma Research is building the brains for robots that keep improving throughout their working lives. Robotics is the first proposed market. The product direction is a supported Cadence runtime and a brain prepared for a customer's embodiment, beginning with a paid evaluation on one adaptation or recovery task.

Cadence 0.70.0 builds one continuing brain. System 1 is the default: perception, plastic connections, a working trace, associative memory, action and private imagination, learning from the measured outcome of each action with no separate training mode. System 2 is optional: observing regions read the brain's own activity and return feedback inside the same settlement. Bounded observer-like, self-reading patches carry local state and records, receive signals through ports, and repair their disagreement together; the settled state supplies the answer. A layout whose patches never settle against one another does not build.

## Company and product

- [Cadence](https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/): architecture, code and simulation evidence.
- [Demonstrations](https://floatingpragma.io/demos/): working applications and experiments from cadence-demos.
- [Interactive brain](https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/#inside-the-brain): switch between the default layout and one with observers, inspect patch state and error, and compare settlement with a forward calculation.
- [Robotics](https://floatingpragma.io/robotics/): proposed evaluation programme and changed-wheel rover experiment.
- [Investors](https://floatingpragma.io/investors/): proposed $4 million seed round over 18 months.

## Code and evidence

- [Official demonstrations](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos): music, games and simulated worlds, with each application's engine and evidence described separately.
- [Open-source core](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence): GPL-3.0-or-later Python package.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/blob/v0.70.0/docs/equilibrium/DRSN.md): the population solver's state-and-error observation within one coupled settlement.
- [Quickstart](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/blob/v0.70.0/docs/quickstart.md): build a small brain.
- [Learning and memory](https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/blob/v0.70.0/docs/continuous.md).
- [Package](https://pypi.org/project/cadence-net/): install cadence-net.
- [Cadence preprint](https://philpapers.org/rec/MUECAP-2).
- [Doom evidence excerpt](https://floatingpragma.io/evidence/cadence/doom-confirmations.json): two reserved Basic-scenario evaluations, source hashes and verification records.
- [CartPole evidence excerpt](https://floatingpragma.io/evidence/cadence/cartpole-confirmations.json): 180 held-out episodes at the 500-step limit with supplied-state teaching.

Simulation evidence establishes bounded behavior under the stated conditions. Physical robot adaptation, a useful advantage from recursive depth, broad retention and electrical energy advantages require separate tests. Evidence excerpts are compact source projections, not complete reproduction bundles.

## Research origin

Observer Patch Holography (OPH) asks whether bounded observers can build a shared physical account from local records, overlap comparison and repair. Its organizing idea inspired Cadence; cortical cooperation supplies another computational inspiration. Formal proofs establish consequences of specified assumptions. A physical or biological interpretation requires its own evidence.

- [Research overview](https://floatingpragma.io/physics/).
- [Research explainer](https://floatingpragma.io/watch/).
- [Main preprints](https://floatingpragma.io/research/#preprints): links to the physics and Cadence preprints.
- [Physics preprint](https://philpapers.org/rec/MUEFOC).
- [Pragma Research Blog](https://blog.floatingpragma.io/).
- [Scientific source](https://github.com/FloatingPragma/observer-patch-holography/).
- [Extended source map](https://floatingpragma.io/llms-full.txt).

## Brain design: System 1 and optional System 2

System 1 is the default brain, composed with Brain.compose; System 2 adds optional observers to the same brain. Every answer is the settled state of the whole brain, and a brain that does not settle refuses to act. Beside the main interface, Cadence 0.70.0 keeps advanced engines with their own contracts: the population solver, where populations of patches settle one joint energy and observers read exact prediction errors; record patches for event records and consolidation; and a temporal model for learned action consequences and planning. System 1 and System 2 name functional roles in software, not claims of biological equivalence. Choose observers by measured task quality, query latency and learning cost; deeper is not automatically better or faster. Archived AMEN uses a record-patch brain trained on an earlier release.

- Research and preprints: https://floatingpragma.io/research/
- Work in physics, mathematics, AI and security: https://floatingpragma.io/work/
- Brain design: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence/blob/v0.70.0/docs/brain.md
- Performance: https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/#design-patterns

## Public demonstrations

The official demonstration source is https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos. The website showcase is https://floatingpragma.io/demos/.

- Atari Arcade: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/atari-arcade/ — a playable browser edition in which fresh Cadence brains learn Freeway and Atlantis from a scripted teacher and rewards, on an Atari 2600 emulator with a JavaScript port of the reference engine; the Python server edition with four games is at https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos/tree/main/atari-arcade.
- AMEN: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/amen/ — a playable archived record-memory composer; fixed learned checkpoint, generated musical events and supplied instrument.
- Patch World: https://floatingpragma.io/demos/patch-world/ — a playable JavaScript artificial-life simulation on the Cadence 0.70 population solver: brains that learn in the browser and evolve their layouts, with observer stages as an optional gene.
- Rover Lab: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence-demos/tree/main/rover-lab — local simulated rover on cadence-net 0.70.0 whose live body model adapts when a wheel weakens, with no separate training mode; a four-patch brain, an optional observer arm, a supplied action selector and declared timing measurements.

The embedded browser applications are copied from a pinned cadence-demos commit; their source and published file hashes are at https://floatingpragma.io/demos/runtime/manifest.json. Their engines differ, so the showcase identifies each mechanism and result separately.
